name: Supplementary which with a Clausal Anchor
pattern: Clause or larger discourse unit + supplement with relative which

entry.name: Supplementary which with a Clausal Anchor
entry.pattern: Clause or larger discourse unit + supplement with relative which

1.definition: Refers back to a situation or proposition conveyed by an anchor.

examples.form: The train had already left, [which was unfortunate].

projection.target: Which can refer to the departure situation as a whole. Number from an incidental NP inside the anchor does not determine the reference of which.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Which pointing back at a whole situation
curious.summary: A which can follow a statement and refer back to the whole situation it describes, not to a single thing in it.
curious.body: In The train had already left, which was unfortunate, the word which doesn't point at the train. It points at the whole situation: the fact that the train had already left. That's what was unfortunate. The pattern is a comment tacked onto the end of a statement. It's a special case of a larger family of add-on remarks that begin with which. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional, so treat the details as a working proposal.

examples.text: The train had already left, [which was unfortunate].
The shop was closed, [which surprised us].

curious.try: Add a which remark to the end of a sentence you just said. What exactly is the which referring to?

teacher.summary: Helps explain why which can refer to a whole preceding statement, not just a noun.
teacher.explain: A supplementary relative clause beginning with which can take as its anchor a clause (or a longer stretch of discourse), not only a noun phrase. In The train had already left, which was unfortunate, which refers to the departure situation as a whole. Number on a noun phrase inside the anchor, such as the singular noun train, doesn't determine what which refers to. This dictionary treats the pattern as a specialization of the ordinary supplementary relative, and marks the analysis as provisional.
teacher.terms: Sometimes called a sentential relative. In this dictionary: supplementary relative with a clausal anchor.

examples.text: The train had already left, [which was unfortunate].
The shop was closed, [which surprised us].

watch_for: A learner might take which to refer only to the nearest noun, such as the train, when it refers to the whole situation.
teacher.activity: Give pairs a short statement on a card. Each student adds a which comment, then partners say aloud what which stands for. Collect a few and discuss which ones refer to the whole situation.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Supplementary which with a Clausal Anchor." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/relative-clausal-which-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
